title: Uniform vanishing on ind-constructible targets
statement:
Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a finite intermediate extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. Use $\underline E$ of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring $\underline{\Qlb}$ of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. Use the pulled-back condensed coefficient ring $\Lambda_X=p_X^*\underline\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and the module category $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], with its ordinary derived category $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ for the module sheaves which, locally on affine opens, admit a finite stratification by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] on each of which they have a finite constant local model [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model]. Write $\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$ for small filtered colimits of these sheaves, computed in $\Mod_{\Lambda_X}$. For sheaves $C,N$ and every $q\in\mathbf Z$, put $\Ext^q(C,N)=\Hom_{D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})}(C[0],N[0][q])$, extending the nonnegative convention [def-pc-ext].

Let $C\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ and fix an integer $d_C\geq0$ which is a uniform constructible Ext bound for $C$: $\Ext^r(C,N)=0$ for every $r>d_C$ and every $N\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ (the property intended by $d_C$ in [sk-lem-uniform-constructible-ext]). For every small filtered diagram $(D_\alpha)$ of constructible sheaves, put $B=\varinjlim_\alpha D_\alpha\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, the natural map induced by the colimit cocone,
$$\varinjlim_\alpha\Ext^q(C,D_\alpha)\longrightarrow\Ext^q(C,B),$$
is an isomorphism. In particular, $\Ext^q(C,B)=0$ for $q>d_C$, for every $B\in\IndCons(X,\Lambda)$.

proof.text: Fix the small filtered diagram in the statement and any integer $q$. Regard every $D_\alpha$ as a complex with its only nonzero term in degree zero. All these complexes vanish below $b=0$, and their termwise colimit has term $B$ in degree zero and zero elsewhere: a colimit of a diagram of zero objects is zero. The colimit cocone is exactly the cocone specified in the statement. This calculation uses only degree-zero complexes, and makes no assertion about categorical colimits in the derived category.

source.place: Opening sentence: degree-zero complexes and their common lower bound

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity] to this diagram. Its scheme hypothesis holds because $X$ is Noetherian as explicitly assumed. Its field-coefficient clause includes both $\underline E$ and $\underline{\Qlb}$ and every constructible sheaf $C$; our modules are over exactly its pulled-back ring $\Lambda_X$. The index category is small and filtered and Step 1 supplies its common lower bound $b=0$. Its canonical Hom comparison therefore gives $\varinjlim_\alpha\Hom(C[0],D_\alpha[0][q])\simeq\Hom(C[0],B[0][q])$. By the Ext convention this is the required map. The cited lemma specifies the map as the one induced by the same cocone, so the identification proves the assertion for the natural map, for any chosen presentation.

source.place: Continuity sentence: comparison for every q; current continuity node, field-coefficient and in-particular clauses

proof.text: If $q>d_C$, each $D_\alpha$ is constructible, so the defining property of the fixed bound $d_C$ gives $\Ext^q(C,D_\alpha)=0$. The colimit of this zero diagram of abelian groups is zero: the zero group has the required unique map to every cocone vertex. Step 2 therefore gives $\Ext^q(C,B)=0$. Every ind-constructible $B$ admits such a small filtered presentation by the definition stated above, so this proves vanishing for every $B$. The existence of a bound is not being deduced from continuity: it is the bound fixed in the statement, as intended by the parent unit.

source.place: Final sentence: termwise vanishing and its filtered colimit
